newsitem.title: UK: JGBs steal the global bond show in January-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: JGBs steal the global bond show in January-Salomon.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) came out on top during January in the Salomon Brothers world government bond index, Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday. Overall the index rose 0.77 percent in local currency terms, 0.87 percent in dollars.
Boosted by falls on the Nikkei stock market, JGBs made gains of 1.33 percent for January and also headed the field in dollar terms, rising by 1.72 percent.

Spanish Bonos also fared well, closely followed by French OATs. Bonos gained 1.23 percent in local currency and 1.11 percent in dollars. OATs made gains of 1.20 percent French francs and a rise of 1.34 percent in dollars.
Elsewhere in Europe, British gilts increased by 1.18 percent, in sterling terms and 1.08 in dollars, while German Bunds rose by 1.10 percent in marks and 1.26 percent in dollars.
Italian BTPs also recorded an increase of 0.99 percent in local currency terms and 0.80 in dollars.
U.S. Treasuries made only modest gains of 0.15 percent.

The only bond markets which failed to show gains in January were Sweden and Canada. Swedish bonds made a 0.01 percent loss in local currency terms, while Canadian bonds fell by 0.10 percent. In U.S. dollar terms they made 0.15 percent and 0.10 percent respectively. Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
